judges: As Also In The Interest Of Both The J.
trial_court: Metropolitan Magistrate No. 12, Jaipur in Criminal case No. 70/2011
case_name: Sumit Garg And Ors vs State Of Rajasthan And Anr

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Sumit Garg and others (husband, wife, etc.)

facts_of_case: Matrimonial dispute between parties; FIR lodged against petitioners for offences under Section 498A IPC, Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act; parties arrived at amicable settlement and compromise submitted before trial court; decree of divorce passed by Family Court No.3, Rohini Courts, Delhi.

legal_principles.principle: It would be in the interest of justice to not allow criminal proceedings to continue when parties have entered into a compromise.
legal_principles.held: After having considered the facts and circumstances of the case as revealed from the material placed on record as well as the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and in view of the fact that the instant case relates to the matrimonial relations between the parties, who have entered into a compromise, it would be in the interest of justice as also in the interest of both the spouses that the present criminal proceeding should not be allowed to continue.

legal_principles.principle: Cordial relations between parties may be strained if criminal proceedings are continued despite a compromise.
legal_principles.held: In case the criminal proceedings are otherwise continued, despite of the compromise, then the cordial relations between the parties, which have developed because of the amicable settlement, may be strained.

outcome.final_order: Criminal proceedings quashed; interest of justice served in allowing parties to move forward with cordial relations.

keywords: High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan at Jaipur Bench
